idiom_name: interface/type alias for the wire shape + JSON.parse (add a schema validator at untrusted boundaries)
implementation_notes: TypeScript's DTO is a type: an interface or type alias describes the payload shape and the runtime value is a plain JSON.parse result, so the classic class with its fields, constructor and methods disappears. That is also the trap - types are erased, so an interface alone guarantees nothing at runtime, and at any untrusted boundary the local idiom is a schema-first validator (zod, valibot, io-ts, ArkType) whose parse produces a checked value with an inferred type. Use the validator as the single source of truth and infer the DTO type from it, instead of maintaining an interface and a schema that drift apart.
pitfalls: A type assertion (JSON.parse(wire) as OrderDTO) is a compile-time lie: nothing is checked, extra fields pass silently and a typo surfaces far away from the boundary.
JSON numbers are double precision, so 64-bit identifiers overflow past 2^53 - model them as strings or a BigInt-safe encoding.

Structural typing means any object with the right fields satisfies the DTO type, and interfaces are erased at runtime, so instanceof-style checks are impossible; derive types from schemas instead of the reverse.
